newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank Leumi rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank Leumi rated a buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers has assigned Bank Leumi, Israel's second-largest commercial bank, a buy rating in a report released on Wednesday.

"The shares are trading below book value -- an attractive valuation in both a developed and developing market context -- and at discounted 1996-98 earnings multiples relative to the European banking sector," said analyst Matthew Czepliewicz.
Salomon said it expected Leumi to continue showing a recovery in "core" earnings that began in 1995 into 1997 and 1998.

Czepliewicz said core earnings would rise six percent after inflation for 1996 to 0.38 shekels per share, despite a big provision for early retirements. Without the provision, earnings per share (EPS) would have shown a 37 percent rise, he added.
Leumi is due to report 1996 earnings around March 31.
In 1997, Czepliewicz said EPS would grow 98 percent to 0.79 shekel, mainly due to capital gains.

He said real return on equity (ROE) would reach 10 percent in 1996. "We forecast a medium-term real ROE exceeding 9.5 percent, despite a Tier 1 capital ratio that stood at 9.8 percent at September 30, 1996," Czepliewicz said.

"One operating item that bears watching is the still high, though improving, level of construction leding," he said. "The recent investment concern in the entire Israeli market regarding the stalled peace process and the air of political stasis appears to have faded."
